summary: Redwood AE/SE team demoed structured-output (JSON mode) and function/tool-calling flow for Stratos AI. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15 - 09:30 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lydia Park (Redwood AE), Aman Singh (Redwood SE), Evan Reyes (CTO, Stratos), Priya Kapoor (Head of ML), Tom Li (Platform), Sara Malik (Security)

[00:00] Lydia Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Lydia, AE at Redwood, with Aman our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Evan Reyes: Good, thanks. excited to see the structured output stuff, we've been looking at schema enforcement for our ingestion pipeline.
[00:14] Lydia Park: Awesome. quick agenda - walk through JSON mode and function/tool calling, show Console traces and Optimize suggestions, then Q&A and next steps. Aman will lead the demo.
[00:25] Aman Singh: Cool - hi all. starting from high level: structured output lets you define a JSON schema and the model will be constrained to produce that shape. we couple that with function-calling so you can trigger downstream tools reliably.
[00:38] Priya Kapoor: when you say "constrained" is that enforcement or post-hoc validation? like do you reject or auto-correct?
[00:44] Aman Singh: good q. we do a mix - primary is schema-guided generation, we also run a validator hook. by default we return a validation error along with the raw assistance so you can decide fallback logic. you can set strict mode to enforce, or a permissive mode which tries to coerce.
[01:02] Tom Li: what's the failure surface look like for downstream services if schema fails? do you get an error code?
[01:08] Aman Singh: yes, the API returns a structured envelope: status, errors, and the last-good payload. if you're using function-calling integration the runtime will not call the tool unless the payload matches; or you can opt for auto-fix attempts with a max-rewrite budget.
[01:22] Sara Malik: from security perspective we need logs of all calls and proof that PII isn't leaked to third parties. how does Redwood handle logs and KMS?
[01:30] Lydia Park: short answer - we store audit logs, you can integrate with your KMS for key management, and Dedicated/Private installs allow you to control retention or disable logs. we'll share SOC2 and KMS docs after.
[01:40] Sara Malik: okay please send that.
[01:42] Evan Reyes: can you show us the Console and a live example of function-calling to our internal tool? we can't share the actual tool but can show a sample endpoint.
[01:50] Aman Singh: absolutely. starting Console - I'm opening the structured-output tab. (typing) Example: we define a JSON schema for customer_record with name, email, account_id, and nested usage array.
[02:05] [02:05] Aman Singh: I'll paste a short prompt and the schema. watch the live validation panel - it highlights missing fields or mismatches.
[02:15] [02:15] Aman Singh: (demo voice) here's a prompt: "Extract customer info from support transcript and emit valid JSON"; model returns JSON that matches schema on first pass in most cases; when it doesn't, Console shows which property failed and a suggested fix.
[02:32] Priya Kapoor: nice - how deterministic is that across different seeds / prompt paraphrases? we need repeatability for nightly ETL.
[02:40] Aman Singh: our evaluation shows schema adherence rates ~94% on our test sets for similar prompts; for higher determinism you can (1) tighten schema (types/enums), (2) use higher temperature control to 0-0.2, (3) leverage function-calling mode which is stricter. Console also surfaces a confidence score per field.
[02:58] Evan Reyes: is that confidence exposed in the API responses?
[03:02] Aman Singh: yes, the API returns a per-field confidence and a top-level validation boolean. example payload in docs.
[03:10] Tom Li: performance - what's the latency hit when using strict schema enforcement and function-calling?
[03:16] Aman Singh: small overhead - typically +15-30ms due to validation and postprocessing, depending on payload size. if you use continuous KV-caching and batching via Optimize recommendations we can offset token costs and latency.
[03:33] Lydia Park: quick note on hosting modes: Hosted API is easiest; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and private networking; Private installs run in your VPC or on-prem with a control-plane we can integrate.
[03:46] Priya Kapoor: for our POC we want to run both Hosted and Dedicated runs to compare latency/cost. is that feasible?
[03:52] Aman Singh: totally - we can set up a short POC where we run identical payloads across hosted and dedicated and capture throughput, p50/p95, and cost per 1M tokens.
[04:02] [04:02] Aman Singh: now switching to function-calling demo - we map JSON output to a tool spec. here's a mock tool: /create-customer which accepts the customer_record schema. I'll demo a failed run and an auto-fix run.
[04:15] [04:15] Aman Singh: first run: model returns email as "evan at stratos dot ai" - Console flags mismatch, shows attempted correction suggestions. in strict mode the call is blocked, in permissive mode we apply normalization.
[04:31] Priya Kapoor: that's helpful - can you configure allow-list and deny-list for fields? e.g., block external URL fields from being called?
[04:38] Aman Singh: yes - guardrails include allow/deny lists, regex checks, and custom validator hooks you can plug in (Lambda-style or webhook).
[04:47] Tom Li: for the webhook validators do you retry? what's the SLA?
[04:50] Aman Singh: retry is configurable; default is two retries with exponential backoff. for Dedicated we can offer higher SLAs and local validators inside VPC to avoid egress.
[04:59] Sara Malik: about data residency - we need EU-only processing for a subset of customers. is region pinning supported?
[05:05] Lydia Park: yes, you can pin region at route level and at model version; Private supports full on-prem. we'll include region options in the SOW.
[05:13] Evan Reyes: can you run a quick live curl example for the function call so my platform team can see the payload and envelope?
[05:18] Aman Singh: sure - switching to terminal. (typing) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"rwd-structured-v1","prompt":"...","json_schema":{...},"function_call":{"name":"/create-customer","arguments_schema":{...}}}' 
[05:40] Aman Singh: response - we show the envelope: {status: "ok", data: {...}, validation: {passed:true, fields: {...}}, invoked_tool: "/create-customer", tool_resp: {code:200}}
[05:55] Priya Kapoor: excellent. can Console also show a replay of the request/response timeline?
[06:00] Aman Singh: yes the request trace pane shows token breakdown, latency by stage (model, validation, webhook), and Optimize suggestions inline.
[06:10] Lydia Park: quick aside on Optimize - it will analyze your traffic and recommend batching parameters, quantization profiles, and caching TTLs for prefixes to reduce per-token cost while maintaining latency.
[06:21] Tom Li: any rough numbers for cost reduction?
[06:24] Aman Singh: varies, but typical wins are 20-50% per-token on production IE workloads using batching + KV prefix cache + int8 quantization. we can run your traces to give precise numbers.
[06:35] Evan Reyes: ok that would be useful.
[06:38] Aman Singh: now demoing guardrail policies - I add a policy that blocks outbound HTTP tool calls unless a header X-Approved:true is present. Console blocks the call and logs the reason.
[06:50] Sara Malik: good. one more security question - do you support SAML SSO and RBAC for teams?
[06:55] Lydia Park: yes, SSO via SAML/Okta, SCIM provisioning, and configurable RBAC roles. Dedicated and Private offer more granular audit log retention.
[07:05] Evan Reyes: timeline - if we wanted to start POC next week, is that realistic?
[07:10] Lydia Park: yes, we can get you set up with a sandbox key and a POC checklist. SE-led benchmark the following week. we'll send SOW draft.
[07:18] Priya Kapoor: for the benchmark we will provide sample payloads and target p95 < 250ms for inference.
[07:24] Aman Singh: noted - we'll include p95 and throughput targets and run both hosted and dedicated profiles.
[07:30] Tom Li: one more: how do you handle model upgrades and rollbacks for pinned routes?
[07:34] Aman Singh: routes can pin model version and have rollout policies - canary percent, automatic rollback on error or quality regression. Console exposes eval diffs per prompt set.
[07:45] Evan Reyes: that eval diff feature is key for us. we need to detect subtle JSON regressions.
[07:50] Aman Singh: yep - you can attach prompt sets and failure conditions; Redwood will alert on regressions.
[07:57] Lydia Park: quick recap and next steps - we'll send the security pack and demo recording, Aman will share the function-calling notebook and curl examples, and we'll propose POC SOW with hosted vs dedicated benchmark. any other open items?
[08:10] Sara Malik: just the firewall/egress question - I'll send a list of endpoints and we'll want egress rules documented.
[08:16] Lydia Park: great - action items and owners noted. thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with timelines.
[08:24] Evan Reyes: thanks, good session.
[08:27] [END]
